title: The Victim Who Came Back
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, the Detective Boys Mitsuhiko/Ayumi/Genta, Inspector Megure, Officer Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: actions are direct typed edges between the people/location/object nodes actually involved. Corrections vs. the old lower-fidelity file: (1) the old file's e3 desc says Tokunaga hid the body 'fearing a local cat burglar might find it in his own room' -- this is Mitsuhiko's theory, which Conan explicitly refutes on-screen ('No. That's impossible, Mitsuhiko.'); the transcript's actual solution is that Tokunaga overheard a police patrol car's public loudspeaker warning about neighborhood burglaries and mistook the general warning for a specific threat to himself, panicking and dumping the sofa+body before his evening shift -- encoded here as the `abandons_body_at` edge's detail, not the cat-burglar theory. (2) the old file's `knows` edges (s1->v1, s2->v1) are unsupported: Hosono explicitly denies knowing the victim ('No, I did not'), and Tokunaga's tie to the victim is a debt relationship, not mere acquaintance -- dropped `knows` in favor of `relationship: debtor_of` and `has_motive_against`. (3) the old file omits Hirose, the recycle-shop worker whose account of the locked delivery truck is what re-anchors the investigation on the Akebono dump/neighborhood -- added as a named person here. (4) old file's culprit (Tokunaga) is confirmed correct by the transcript; his confession names the debt/bar-license threat as motive, added here. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Tokunaga's claim of overhearing an argument through the wall is contradicted by a theater employee confirming Hosono's alibi during that exact window -- revealing his testimony as a deliberate lie to frame her.
Victim found without shoes despite the body surfacing at an outdoor dump/sofa -- she was killed indoors and moved, not killed where found.

The recycle truck was locked immediately after the sofa was loaded and stayed locked until delivery, so the body was already inside before the shop's 4 PM pickup -- pushing the crime back to the dump itself.
